microsoft.guideAzure: Sign in to Azure. If this is your first visit, complete sign-up using “Start” under “Start with an Azure free trial”. This prepares a directory (tenant), the space where you register your app. Use your existing directory if you have one.
microsoft.guideTenantError: If an error says your account does not exist in the “Microsoft Services” tenant, including an “Interaction required” dialog with that message, do not keep retrying sign-in. microsoft.register: On the Azure home page, select “Manage Microsoft Entra ID → View”. In “Default Directory”, expand “Manage → App registrations” on the left, then select “+ New registration” at the top.
microsoft.guideAccounts: Enter “Vyact” as the name. Select “All Entra ID tenants + personal Microsoft accounts” as the supported account type. Leave the redirect URI blank and select “Register”.
microsoft.guideRedirect: Copy the “Application (client) ID” after registration. Open “Add a Redirect URI → Add a platform → Mobile and desktop applications”. Paste {{redirectUri}} into the custom URI field and select “Configure”. Leave the three preset URI checkboxes unchecked. You do not need to add a certificate or secret.
microsoft.guidePermissions: Add delegated Graph permissions: User.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, Calendars.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite. Company policies may require administrator consent.
microsoft.guideClient: Return to this settings page in Vyact. Paste the copied ID into “Application (client) ID” below and select “Save”. Select “+ Add Microsoft account → Connect”, sign in with the Outlook account you want to use, and consent to the requested permissions. If an account card already exists, select “Connect” directly. Your email address appears on the card once connected.

mcpDefaultPrompts.custom:
Context7 Usage Rules (example for @upstash/context7-mcp)
For requests involving libraries, APIs, frameworks, or docker-compose, call the Context7 MCP first.
Do not generate code before checking Context7.
mcpDefaultPrompts.github:
GitHub Code Changes and Pull Request Rules
When asked to change code in a GitHub repository or create a pull request:
1. Use get_file_contents to inspect the current file and SHA.
2. Create a working branch with create_branch from the default branch.
3. Commit changes with create_or_update_file, passing the previously retrieved SHA. Use push_files for multiple files.
4. Create the pull request with create_pull_request and clearly describe what changed and why.

Always inspect files before changing them, show the proposed changes before committing, and use list_branches when the default branch is unknown. For code-review requests, review the retrieved code without modifying it.
mcpDefaultPrompts.sequential_thinking:
Sequential Thinking Usage Rules
Use the sequential thinking tool for tasks requiring multi-step reasoning, such as debugging, architecture design, root-cause analysis, investment decisions, and complex comparisons. Break the reasoning into stages, review previous conclusions, and revise them when necessary before reaching the final answer.
Do not use it for simple factual questions, short answers, or requests completed with a single lookup.
mcpDefaultPrompts.google_workspace:
Google Workspace Usage Rules
Use the available Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Slides, and Google Forms tools according to the user's request.

Search for and verify the relevant data before taking action. Handle recipients, titles, content, dates, times, attendees, locations, files, folders, and permissions accurately. Preserve the user's timezone and use ISO 8601 for calendar times; do not invent a time when it is unclear. Ask for clarification when the target is ambiguous. Confirm the scope before important changes or deletions, perform multi-step work in the required order, and clearly summarize the result.
